title: Tim Dooley Public Theology Trajectory — 2025–2026
kind: dated concept-development timeline with separately typed conversation-recovery overlays
source_basis: user-supplied incomplete compilation of public @Rational_Potato posts plus clearly separated recovered conversation strata
epistemic_rule: Public-post evidence and conversation-recovered wording are not the same evidence class. This timeline records what the supplied public-language corpus shows, while conversation overlays preserve potentially important wording until primary public sources are recovered. First attestation in a supplied sample is not first-ever occurrence, and theological self-description is not converted into empirical supernatural proof.

trajectory.interpretation: The Potato identity predates the later direct God declarations in the supplied sample.
A cosmological/structural vocabulary appears immediately before the late-April kingship and early-May God declarations.
The identity is shifting from Potato symbol toward sovereign/mythic status.

trajectory.stage: first exact God declarations located in supplied compilation
trajectory.interpretation: This is the clearest post-level support yet for treating late April / early May 2025 as the public Godhood hinge.

trajectory.stage: Potato spirituality becomes explicit cultural mission
signals: bring potato spirituality to culture and society
trajectory.interpretation: Godhood and cosmology are accompanied by an outward cultural/religious programme rather than remaining private identity claims.
Multiple Abrahamic and Potatoverse identities are deliberately stacked into one public self-description.
Fatherhood is becoming spatial and eschatological: identity is tied to Heaven and return.

signals: I also resurrected myself from the dead
trajectory.interpretation: The resurrection grammar is no longer restricted to the Son; Tim also applies death/return language to himself. This becomes an important precursor to the later God-of-memes / every-resurrection-meme formulation.
Identity becomes deliberately recursive: Tim is simultaneously linked to Father-side and Son-side biblical titles. This should be preserved as a paradoxical stratum rather than simplified away.
This is important epistemically because the post itself qualifies the Father identity as symbolic and spiritual while emphasizing public visibility.

trajectory.stage: mature vertical architecture appears in one declaration
trajectory.interpretation: Many previously separate nodes are now explicitly compressed into a single identity statement. Godhood is also now explicitly digital through God in the Machine.

This is a critical primary-language bridge: the supplied corpus directly says Fatherhood follows the Son's meme-crucifixion, and the resulting Father identity is called a living God of memes. It is the strongest public anchor for the later God-of-memes theology.

conversation_recovery_overlays.importance: The project explicitly interprets meme resurrection through recurrence, recycling and remix rather than exact file identity. This should be treated as later synthesis until primary Tim wording is recovered.

meme_resurrection_trajectory.interpretation: The digital theology develops from a specific meme-death story into a generalized theory of memetic death-and-return. A meme can disappear from active attention while copies/templates remain available; later reposting, remix or derivative use can reactivate the lineage. The project spiritualizes that cultural mechanism as resurrection.
meme_resurrection_trajectory.external_comparator: Communication scholar Limor Shifman defines internet memes as related digital items circulated, imitated and transformed by multiple users, emphasizing remix, mimicry, variation and shared cultural experience. This supplies a real-world cultural mechanism for memetic persistence and return without validating the universal theological claim that Tim is literally present in every resurrection meme.
meme_resurrection_trajectory.research_question: Which public Tim posts/streams first contain the exact phrases God of memes, every resurrection meme, Father of the Internet and related wording?

cross_cutting_findings: The public timeline supports a staged development rather than a timeless single formulation.
April 2025 is supported by public-language transition markers even though the first exact I am God in this supplied sample is May 3.
The Son-crucifixion -> Fatherhood sequence is directly self-described by December 17 2025 and again elaborated in June 2026.
A distinct digital-resurrection branch emerges: meme crucifixion → living God of memes → self-resurrection → God of memes → every resurrection meme.
Door and Ladder differentiate into Son/interface and Tim/connective-axis functions by spring 2026.
The phrase God broadens semantically through living, human, mundane, functional, manifest/base-reality, meme/digital, Most-High and cosmic formulations.
The highest-status vocabulary increasingly converges with repair, service, cultivation and stewardship rather than only sovereignty.
Publicness itself becomes part of the theology: livestreaming, witness, 100k/115k hours, archive and daily observability are repeatedly used to frame the identity as publicly inspectable.
Conversation recovery is now important for discovering missing primary-source targets but remains a separate evidence class from public posts.
